questions.prompt: A smoke test answers which question?
options: Is every feature correct?
Is this build stable enough to be worth testing further?
Has performance improved?
Which defects were fixed?
questions.explanation: A smoke test is a short gate on the main functions. It does not try to prove full correctness or measure performance.

questions.prompt: A good smoke suite is short, stable and covers the most critical paths.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Smoke tests must run quickly and give a trustworthy go/no-go signal, so they focus on a few critical, stable checks.

questions.prompt: Which check is least suitable for a smoke suite of an online bank?
options: Customer can log in
Account balance page loads
A transfer between own accounts completes
Every validation message on the address change form has the correct wording
questions.explanation: Detailed wording checks belong in feature or regression testing. Login, balances and a core transfer are critical paths that decide whether deeper testing is possible.

questions.prompt: A hotfix changes only the password-reset email template. In common industry usage, what is a sanity check here?
options: Run the full regression suite
A narrow check that the reset email is sent with the corrected template and its link works
Run only performance tests
No testing is needed for a template
questions.explanation: Many teams use 'sanity' for a narrow check focused on the changed area. Full regression is broader than needed for this purpose; skipping testing is risky because templates break links and variables.

questions.prompt: How does the ISTQB glossary treat the term 'sanity test'?
options: As a type of performance test
As a synonym of smoke test
As a synonym of acceptance test
It does not mention it
questions.explanation: The ISTQB glossary lists sanity test as a synonym for smoke test. Industry usage often differs, which is why teams should agree their own terms.

questions.prompt: A smoke suite has grown to 180 checks, takes 2 hours and often fails on minor UI changes. What went wrong?
options: Nothing; more checks give more confidence
It has become a regression suite: it lost the short, stable, critical-path focus a smoke gate needs
The tests should be run manually instead
The build server is too slow
questions.explanation: A smoke suite that is long and brittle can no longer act as a fast gate. Trim it to the critical paths and move the rest to regression.

questions.prompt: A smoke test fails because nobody can log in. What should a build rejection include? Select all that apply.
options: The build/version identifier
The failed check with steps and evidence (screenshot, logs, request ID)
A notification to the build owner or team channel
Starting the 200 scheduled regression tests anyway to save time
questions.explanation: Rejection should be traceable and actionable: which build, what failed, proof and who is told. Running regression on a build that cannot log in wastes effort and produces noise.

questions.prompt: A smoke run fails on 'search returns results' only. Login, cart and checkout pass. Release testing for a payments change is the main goal of this cycle. What is the most sensible decision?
options: Reject the build automatically, whatever failed
Accept it silently because payments work
Raise the search failure with evidence and let the agreed rule decide; if the team's rule allows, continue payments testing while search is fixed, recording the risk
Mark search as passed since it is not in scope
questions.explanation: Build-rejection rules should be agreed in advance. A visible, recorded decision is better than either blind rejection or silently ignoring the failure. Marking a failure as passed is falsifying results.

questions.prompt: Your team argues for a week about whether a 15-check suite is 'smoke' or 'sanity'. What is the most productive action?
options: Adopt the ISTQB definition and refuse other usages
Agree and write down what each term means for this team (purpose, scope, when it runs, who decides) and move on
Rename both to 'regression'
Stop running the suite until the debate ends
questions.explanation: The lesson's advice is to clarify team terminology rather than argue. The value is in a shared definition of purpose and scope, not in winning the naming debate.
